summary:
An English market-town chandlery. Facing the street is a red-brick shop storey with a projecting candle-filled bay window and a separate family door. Above it is a jettied dark-oak and calcite half-timbered storey under a 45° slate gable with two dormers and an east-gable chimney. Behind it are a brick workshop with its own tall rendering-hearth chimney, an open drying lean-to for the candle racks, and a beehive garden that supplies the wax, so the street front reads as a shop, house and workshop all at once. English market-town chandlery: red-brick ground storey on a stone plinth with a five-wide candle bay, a jettied dark-oak/calcite upper storey under a 45° slate roof with two dormers, and a brick east chimney.
Behind it stand a brick workshop with a signal-fire rendering chimney, an open drying lean-to with candle racks, and a back garden of beehives behind a picket fence.
Six trade-cut parts; seven rooms; elements.md and the plan.md sections are written.

Masonry shell: parts/shell.mjs builds the stone plinth, brick walls for the house and workshop, quoins, a stripped-oak head beam over the front, and the floors (y=1 and y=6 with the stairwell hole). It also builds the partitions, the four-step dark oak stair and every opening. The reserved cells stay air. make.sh gives 615 cells for this part with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. All seven rooms are reachable, but I only read the walk output for the first three.
polish: Stairs: the cells under the stair at x=16 are open air, and I did not look at them in a render. I also did not run the render or tile review, only check and walk.
I built the front head beam myself: stripped_dark_oak_wood axis x at (6..16, 5, 8). The plan assigns it to no part, so the facade part should not rebuild it.
I built a stone_brick_slab (top) sill outside the kitchen window at (18,2,14..15).
Upstairs I added partitions: spruce_planks at z=13 with doorways at x=8 and x=13 (y=7..8), and at x=11 for z=14..16. The ground partition at x=12 is dark_oak_planks.
The transom (7,4,8) and the lintel cells at (17,4,11..12) are left as air for fittings and chimneys. Door, window and firebox cells are all air.

Lintel arches over the doors and windows, which I left as plain brick.

summary:
Timber frame: Timber frame built in parts/frame.mjs: sill beam y=6 and head plate y=10 on all four faces, posts, jetty brackets, mirrored front braces, calcite panels, and the upper window holes left as air for P4.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the frame placed 196 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette, and check shows no floating or unsupported blocks. The front reads as dark frame on white daub.
The gable frames at x=5 and x=17 placed nothing: the roof's calcite already fills those cells, so the king posts, collars and the gable windows are missing (see left).
polish: Gable triangles at x=5 and x=17 (y 11..15): the roof part's calcite fills them before the frame runs, so gableFrame's king posts, collars and the window cells (5,12,14) and (17,12,14) were skipped silently. Fix is in the roof spec: keep those cells as air so gableFrame can fill them. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
West wall z=11..12 has one diagonal brace rising north to the post at z=10, not the two-brace Mann figure the plan names. A second brace would need a z-axis brace helper, which vocab lacks.
Upper front and east/west windows (y=8..9) are left as air for the fittings part to glaze; the east gable window is calcite until the roof gap is fixed.
Helpers skip non-air cells silently, and runParts reports refused=0 for the frame even though four gable cells were lost. Checking the frame by eye was the only way I found it.

waste.what: Found the lost gable cells by probing each cell of the built grid one by one with a throwaway script, to learn that the roof's calcite had won.
waste.cost: one probe script, about 16 cell reads, plus a zoom render
waste.tool: A report from gableFrame/framePanel (and runParts) that lists cells skipped because they were not air, with the blocking block and part name; or `mcd cell build.nbt x,y,z`.

waste.what: Wrote a local plane-x panel fill (sidePanel) and a local brace for the west wall by hand, since the vocab helpers only take the z plane (framePanel) or the x run (braceStair, w/e).
waste.cost: about 40 lines of coordinates and one hand-set brace (3 stairs) for the west wall
waste.tool: vocab: framePanel and braceStair with an axis argument (plane x, and n/s rise), so side walls use the same helpers as the front.

waste.what: Worked out the front brace and window-hole coordinates from the plan table by hand (which cells are braced, calcite, or hole in each bay).
waste.cost: about 20 cells checked by reading the plan table
waste.tool: A plan-to-cells table in plan.json (bay list: x range, y range, kind = brace/panel/hole) that the frame builder reads.

companions.task: Agree who owns the gable triangles at x=5 and x=17: the roof part keeps those cells as air (or as a keep box) so the framer's king post, collar and gable window can go in.
Set the upper window panes in the air holes at y=8..9 on the front, back and side walls, and the gable window at (17,12,14), once the frame's calcite is in place.

summary:
Roofs: parts/roofs.mjs lays the main slate roof (roof.json, dormers, keep for the east stack), the workshop gable roof (ridge y=10 along z, keep for the main back wall and rendering stack) via the roof library's roof(), and the lean-to dark-oak slab roof by hand (z=18..25).
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt: Roofs 234 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check reports walkable with 0 floating or unsupported blocks; the front-left and back views read as slate roofs with the lean-to beneath the eave.
Two warnings stay on the workshop roof by design (north overhang 0 per plan; an 11-cell slope with no break). The plan gives no dormer or monitor for it, so that needs the architect's word.
polish: Workshop roof still prints ROOF_NO_OVERHANG (north 0, as plan.md ROOFS specifies where the wing butts the main back wall) and ROOF_BIG_PLANE (unbroken 11-cell slope, no dormer or monitor in the plan). Left as the plan gives them; a break needs the architect's decision.

The main roof's calcite gable fill covers the x=5 and x=17 gable triangles (y 11..15). The timber frame's gableFrame members there will be refused as writes into earlier cells, so the framer must place its king posts and collar on top of the roof's calcite or the plan's gable spec must change.
The workshop ridge uses spruce_slab (the roof tool's choice for ridge: slab), which reads as a pale wood cap on the slate. Confirm, or pick another palette slab.
Lean-to slabs (x=15..19, y=4..5, z=18..25) are laid by this part. leanToBay in vocab also writes that slab course, so the grounds part should lay only the posts or accept refused duplicate writes.

waste.what: Reading the roof library source to find that roof() takes the spec's keys as options and that reroof() strips old roof cells, to decide how to lay the second (workshop) roof when runParts takes only one roof.json.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls of source reading
waste.tool: A build-library helper such as runParts(roof: [spec, ...]) or a roof.json array, so several roofs go through runParts with their own keep boxes and refusal report.

waste.what: Finding the workshop/main junction clash by reading make.sh's REFUSED line (2 cells at z=18, y=10..11 where the main south eave already sits) and then adding a keep box by hand.
waste.cost: 2 make runs and 1 dry-run
waste.tool: roof --dry-run should list the cells it would refuse against earlier parts, not only the warnings.

waste.what: Tile inspection by eye: viewing back, front and front-left renders to confirm the lean-to and the two roofs read correctly.
waste.cost: 3 image reads
waste.tool: A per-part render crop (roofs only, with the shell ghosted) would show the part on its own.

waste.what: Zsh word-splitting of $MCD (a variable holding 'node path') broke three commands, costing retries.
waste.cost: 3 failed commands
waste.tool: A plain mcd shim on PATH (or a note in the kit that $MCD must be called as an absolute node command under zsh).

companions.task: Check the ridge course and the verges on the main and workshop roofs, and pick the ridge slab so it matches the slate rather than the spruce_slab the tool chose.
Hand over the lean-to's posts and wall plate, and the king post and collar members on the x=5 and x=17 gables, which the calcite roof fill currently blocks.

summary:
Openings and fittings: P4 built in parts/fittings.mjs: the shop bay with its candle shelf, four doors with steps, the family-door hood, the transom and every glazed window, upper side shutters, window boxes, the fascia sign, the hanging sign on its fence arm, and the family-door lantern (124 blocks, no refused or off-palette writes).
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; front zoom reads correctly (bay, doors, transom, sign, lantern). Upper-storey pieces float only because the timber frame (P2) is still a stub.
Candles on the shop shelves and counter are left to room-1; plan.md's Notes now record the vocab NBT bug and the kitchen sill issue.
polish: Candle clusters on the shop shelves and counter are not built (elements 'Candles for sale' stays unticked); only the bay shelf candles are in P4. These belong to room-1 (Shop).

Upper-storey pieces float in `$MCD check` only because the timber frame (P2) is a stub: the upper windows' glass, the two upper shutter pairs, the window-box sills, the hanging-sign fence arm and the lantern's support beam at (16,6,7). They should resolve when P2 lands; not verified in a full build.
Shell's kitchen window sill stone_brick_slab (18,2,14..15) has nothing under it at (18,1,14..15) and floats; it is P1's cell, noted in plan.md Notes.
Family door hood at (15,4,7) is flagged as an ORPHAN by check (one face on the brick at (15,4,8)). That is the intended overhang, not a fault.

Upper side shutters sit one cell out from the wall (x=18 east, x=4 west) rather than flat in the wall plane, because the frame's posts occupy the wall-plane flanks. A render check of their facing (open trapdoor, spruce) has not been done.
honeycomb_block accent on the shelves is not built (it belongs with the room shelves).

waste.what: Transcribed every window's glass by hand from plan.md OPENINGS and wrote a pane-connection state per cell (east/west for z-plane walls, north/south for x-plane walls) in local glazeZ/glazeX/pane loops.
waste.cost: about 45 pane coordinates worked out by hand; one wrong plane choice would show only in a render
waste.tool: a build-library `glazing(g, box, plane)` or a vocab helper that takes a list of window boxes and sets connection states from the wall plane; `$MCD plan`-style listing of OPENINGS as data would save the transcription

waste.what: The vocab `put()` helper drops the block-entity NBT, so `wallSign` writes a sign with no text. I had to bypass it and call `B.sign` with `g.set` myself, twice.
waste.cost: 2 retries of reasoning, about 10 minutes of reading vocab source
waste.tool: fix vocab h3.mjs `put()` to pass `nbt` through (`g.set(x,y,z,block,state,nbt)`); the same fix makes wallSign keep its text

waste.what: `hangingSignArm` (elements item and vocabulary item 11) is not exported from any vocab share; I wrote the fence arm, hanging sign and candle locally in fittings.mjs.
waste.cost: one local helper, about 8 lines
waste.tool: add hangingSignArm to vocab h2/h3 as the spec describes it, so the arm, sign and candle come from one call

waste.what: Checked the front and the bay visually by zooming and reading the tile, then used `$MCD check` by eye to separate the floats caused by stub parts from real faults.
waste.cost: 3 check and zoom runs, 1 render
waste.tool: a `mcd check --ignore-parts` mode or a per-part check that only reports floats involving the part's own cells

waste.what: Ticked seven items across elements.md and the plan checklist by hand, each with a separate Edit, and added Notes lines to plan.md.
waste.cost: 8 Edit calls
waste.tool: a `mcd tick <part>` command that marks the checklist and the elements whose lines name that part

companions.task: Hand over the shutter placement and the hanging sign on its fence arm, so the trapdoors lie flat to the wall face and the sign hangs from the arm end, not from a stand-in fence.
Check the pane connection states on the upper front and side windows once the frame is in, and confirm the 1x1 gable panes read as glazing and not as posts.
Fix the kitchen window sill at (18,2,14..15) (it floats over air at (18,1,z)) and the stone hood over the family door, so both sit on a plinth or wall face.

summary: Chimneys and hearths: ["parts/chimneys.mjs builds both stacks and their fireboxes: the east house stack (x18..19, z11..12, y1..19) with the kitchen firebox, and the workshop rendering stack (x8..9, z28..29, y1..13) with its hay-fed signal campfire and firebox.", "make.sh saved a whole build.nbt: chimney part placed 128, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks; the back elevation shows both stacks rising above the roof with the campfire tops.", "Ticked P5 in plan.md and the three chimney/hearth items in elements.md."]
polish: The firebox mouth floor cells (17,1,11..12) and (8..9,1,27) sit in the shell's plinth row; they are not written here and were not verified in the render.
The workshop cauldron that stands in front of the rendering firebox at (8..9,2,26) is a room part's job, not written here.

companions.task: Check where the east stack and the workshop stack pass through the main and workshop roofs (keep boxes, verges meeting the brick), so the roof stays whole around each stack.
Lay the stone floor and plinth under the firebox mouths at (17,1,11..12) and (8..9,1,27), which belong to the shell, and check the lintel bearings at y=4.

summary:
Grounds and lean-to: parts/grounds.mjs builds the street rows, east passage, yard path, herb strip, front and yard fences with gates, four hives and the bee flower bed, woodpile, tallow barrels and cauldron, apple tree, and the drying lean-to floor, posts, slab shed course, two candle racks and barrels.
make.sh runs whole with 394 placed by this part and no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; mcd walk reports every room ok, and mcd check reports one orphan oak leaf at (2,4,20).
plan.md checklist P6 and the six matching elements.md items are ticked, and two Notes lines record the fence corner at x=19 and the shed course on non-post rows.
polish: Orphan oak leaf at (2,4,20) reported by mcd check: one leaf touches the build on one face. Cosmetic; fix by removing that leaf or moving the crown.

Lean-to candle racks and barrels are placed but not walk-checked inside the room in detail: mcd walk says the whole build is walkable and the rooms are ok, but the drying lean-to room's floor was not checked with mcd room.
The apple tree's crown is wider than the yard view suggests; not checked from a close-up tile.

waste.cost: two Read calls on the iso tiles

waste.tool: mcd states/helper docstrings that say the cell each piece occupies (e.g. 'shelf at top of y')

companions.task: Hive orientation and forage: where the four hives face and how the flower bed is laid out so the bees have a flight path and a continuous bloom.
Apple tree crown shape and clearance from the workshop roof, so the crown does not leave orphan leaves on the eave.

summary:
room: Shop: Shop interior built in parts/room-1.mjs: counter at z=14 (dark oak planks, candles and a honeycomb accent on top), barrel shelves with candles on the west and south walls, a stair stool, and three hanging lanterns.
room check says OK: 48 of 48 floor cells reachable, minimum light 8, no dark or dim cells. make.sh saved a whole build.nbt, with no refused writes or off-palette blocks; structure check shows no floating blocks.
Counter top is planks with candles at y=3, not a slab (a slab would float); noted in plan.md Notes. The bay's sill shelf sits at z=8, outside this room's box, so it is left to fittings.
polish: The bay display on its sill shelf (dark_oak_slab at (10..12,2,8) with candles) is outside the Shop box at z=8 and belongs to the fittings part (P4), not built here.
Elements.md item 'Candles for sale' is only partly met: the shop shelves and counter are done, the bay shelf is still open. Left unticked.
Planned trapdoor shelves and slab counter top were replaced by barrel and plank shelves with candles on top, because slabs there would float or could not carry candles; noted in plan.md Notes.
The render check was done on the room view only (room.png, from above and inside); the street tiles from make's render were not inspected.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture and candle cell by hand from the floor grid, then checked support and reachability by trial: a top slab at y=3 would float, and a bottom slab cannot carry a candle.
waste.cost: about 3 rebuild and check cycles, about 30 cells placed by hand through layers
waste.tool: A support-aware helper (for example a counter() or shelf() variant that stacks a candle-bearing top on a full block) plus a 'supports' check in mcd room that flags floating furniture before the render.

waste.what: Found the lantern spot for the dim doorway lane by reading the light grid digits and placing one lantern by hand.
waste.cost: 2 make and room cycles
waste.tool: mcd room already suggests lamp spots; a --apply flag that writes the suggested lantern (hung from the ceiling block) would have saved the rebuild.

waste.what: Checked the shell's floor material at (8,1,12) with a one-off node snippet to confirm spruce_planks.
waste.cost: 1 command
waste.tool: mcd info or mcd blocks-at x,y,z for a single-cell lookup.

companions.task: Build the counter and the wall shelves, to settle the slab-top versus full-block choice and the shelf heights before the candles were placed.
Plan the hanging lantern spots and the candle light levels against the walk lanes, instead of finding the dim doorway lane by trial.

summary:
room: Family hall and kitchen: Family hall and kitchen furnished in parts/room-2.mjs (16 blocks via one layers() call, 4 layers): a kitchen wall with barrel, smoker and furnace (lit) by the hearth, a spruce-fence table with a spruce slab top, a potted poppy, three dark oak stair seats, a white carpet rug, and three hanging lanterns.
make.sh is whole; room check says OK: 33/33 floor cells reachable, min light 9 with no dark cells; parts-report shows 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check reports 0 floating.
The room tool's ASCII view and room.png (from above) read as a furnished kitchen with the table central and the lanes open.
polish: No tick applies: plan.md's checklist has P1..P6 only and elements.md has no Family hall item, so nothing was ticked.
The back door's inside cell (16,2,16) is the shell's stair foot, so the back door opens onto a stair step rather than a floor cell; the walk verdict still reaches it, but the shell should know.

The room is lit by its own lanterns and the furnace/smoker only; the kitchen firebox campfire at (18,2,11..12) is the chimney part's and is not yet built in this copy, so the hearth's glow is not counted yet.

waste.what: Worked out the layout cell by cell from the plan grid: which x/z are free, which are headroom-blocked, where each bench faces and each lantern hangs above a y=6 floor cell.
waste.cost: about 40 cell decisions by hand, one room check to verify.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --furnish` option that proposes a layout from the room's use list (focal piece, seats, lanes) and emits the layers() rows with lantern spots already placed.

waste.what: Chose lantern and lamp spots by guess, then confirmed them with the room check's light grid rather than deriving them from it.
waste.cost: one retry avoided only by luck; the light numbers came back fine.
waste.tool: `mcd room --suggest-lights` writing the lantern cells as layers() rows, so the designer draws them with the furniture in one pass.

companions.task: Light the hearth-side corners and the back-door approach from a lantern plan, so the dimmest cells (the south-west corner, z 15..16) are lit without a second check.
Check the shell's interior stair: its foot at (16,2,16) sits inside the back door, and the steps above have air under them; a joiner would fix the stair before anything else is fitted around it.

summary:
room: Chandler's workshop: Chandler's workshop furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: moulding bench and stool on the north-west wall, barrels with lanterns and candles along the west and east walls, two candle vats and a dipping wheel in the middle, a grindstone, and two tallow cauldrons in front of the south hearth.
make.sh is green with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part, and `mcd room` reports OK: walk ok, min light 8, 0 dark cells. Both views were rendered and read.
The part is finished. The hearth firebox and campfire belong to the chimney part and were not yet in the build when the light was measured.
polish: The light measurement was taken before the chimney part's firebox and campfire at (8..9,2..3,27..28) existed. Once they are built the hearth should add about 13-15 light in the south of the room, so the figures will only improve.

Five floor cells at z=24 (x=7, 8, 9, 10, 11) sit under the dipping wheel's bar, so their headroom is blocked. The walk verdict is still OK because the room is reached from x=6 and x=12, but the floor grid shows those cells blank rather than reachable.
plan.md's checklist has no room entries (only P1..P6), so there was nothing to tick there. In elements.md I ticked the dipping vats and wheel item, which this part built.

Not built on purpose: the workshop's west and east windows and the doorway come from other parts, and the shell-side door at (13,2..3,21) is left for the openings part. The lane from the north doorway (10,18) is kept clear down x=10.

waste.what: Worked out the floor-grid layout by hand, one character per cell, then checked lanes and light by reading the room check output.
waste.cost: About 3 manual passes over the grid plus one rebuild to add the stool and grindstone.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --draw` mode that accepts furniture rules (e.g. 'counter along north wall', 'barrel every 3 cells on west wall', 'keep lane x=10') and emits the layers() rows, so the lane and light rules are checked as it draws.

waste.what: Chose light spots by hand from the light grid, guessing where a lantern on a barrel top would go.
waste.cost: Two guesses at lantern spots; the room check confirmed them with no extra iteration.
waste.tool: `mcd room` should print the chosen lantern cells as ready-to-paste helper calls, not just the spots that would clear the dark.

waste.what: Looked up the tool API by hand, e.g. the lantern state format and the stair facing for a seat, from the library source.
waste.cost: One grep and one read of the build library.
waste.tool: A short reference card for the state formats (lantern hanging as string, stair facing as back side) in the toolkit doc.

companions.task: Lay out the barrels and their candle or lantern tops along the walls and decide which can be a lane and which holds stock.
Check the cauldron, chain and wheel-bar arrangement and what each vat should hold at the hearth, so the dipping wheel reads as a working piece rather than a decorative one.
Place the lights and judge each cell's brightness at floor level, so no corner of the workshop is dark once the chimney firebox is in place.

summary:
room: Drying lean-to: Drying lean-to furnished (parts/room-4.mjs, 14 blocks via layers()): two candle racks on the east side (dark-oak fence uprights, trapdoor shelves, lit white_candle clusters) as the focal piece, tallow barrels with lit candles at the back-west, two hanging lanterns over the racks.
make.sh is green with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; $MCD room says OK: 26 of 26 floor cells reachable, min light 10, 0 dark cells.
The lantern-support and rack-collision problems below depend on the Grounds part, which is still a stub here.
polish: The two hanging lanterns at (17,3,20) and (17,3,23) hang from the lean-to slab roof at y=4 (Grounds part). `mcd check` reports them UNSUPPORTED until that roof is built; if the roof never lands they float.

Candle racks at x=17 (z 19..24) and the barrels at x=15 may collide with Grounds' own leanToBay posts or candleRack calls (posts at x=18, z=18/21/24). Any overlapping cell is refused in runParts and will be reported by the merge; the designer's layout is otherwise unaffected.
The lean-to floor (podzol and coarse_dirt) sits at y=0, outside this room's box, so it is not written here; it belongs to Grounds.
Elements.md's 'Drying lean-to with racks' item is shared with P6 and stays unticked: the posts, roof and racks are Grounds' to build.

waste.tool: A `mcd room --suggest-layout` (or a plan mode that prints lane cells and free rack slots) would have fixed the layout in one pass.

waste.what: I could not use candleRack() for the lit racks, because it hardcodes lit:false, so I drew the racks as text with layers() instead.
waste.cost: one extra legend and one extra layer of text; no retries

make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; the Parlour line shows 28 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check reports no floating or unsupported blocks; room.png read and it reads as a room.

summary:

`$MCD room` says OK: 14 of 17 standable cells reached, min light 8, 0 dark cells. make.sh is green with 13 blocks placed, no REFUSED or off-palette, and the structure check is clean for this room.
The room view (room.png) reads as a bedroom: bed as focal piece, lane kept clear from the doorway at (8,14).

Not checked by eye at a player's height from inside the room. The check and the cutaway view were the only looks.
plan.md and elements.md have no checklist item for the room interiors, so nothing was ticked.

waste.tool: `mcd plan --only <room>` could print a per-layer grid labelled with the absolute (x,y,z) of each row and column, so the row/axis order is visible while drawing. A `layers` dry-run that prints the cell list it would write would also catch this before make.sh.
